author: Barry Yeoman
description:
Suit that cites 2025 Guardian investigation alleges ‘pattern of inaccurate pricing’ that ‘affects millions of purchases’

The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states have sued Dollar General, the nation’s largest dollar-store chain, for persistently overcharging customers at its more than 20,000 stores across the United States.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Nashville, cites a Guardian investigation published last December.

Continue reading...
title: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General, accusing bargain chain of overcharging customers

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
California counties were told by DoJ to set aside and verify ballots administration claims belong to noncitizen voters

A ⁠US appeals court on Monday ruled against Donald ⁠Trump’s ​justice department in a major voting dispute ahead ⁠of the midterm elections, denying a ⁠request to block California from ​counting ‌mail ballots ‌from people on a list ‌of more than 20,000 registered voters the federal government alleges are likely noncitizens.

The decision by ‌the San Francisco-based ninth US circuit court of appeals marked the latest setback in Trump’s efforts to assert ⁠a greater federal role in ​overseeing ​elections in ​the run-up to the 3 ​November midterms ​in ​which his fellow Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress.

Continue reading...
title: Court blocks bid by Trump DoJ to stop California from counting mail-in ballots

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Last Ditch bar announced it would ‘soft close’ after it went viral following a story on its attempt to relax Covid rules

A Massachusetts lesbian bar that went viral for loosening its Covid mask policy last month announced plans to “soft close” on Monday as it seeks new ownership.

The Last Ditch bar, in the small city of Greenfield, said in an Instagram post that it was searching for co-owners, new owners or a full sale, and that it would “soft close effective immediately”, with “only booked events” continuing while it closes this winter. It had opened just last year as a bar for “dykes, transsexuals, gender freaks, workers, and their friends”.

Continue reading...
title: Massachusetts lesbian bar makes frantic effort to find new owners after relaxing masking policy

author: Maya Yang
description:
His comments come ahead of the November midterm elections and follow his claims of widespread voter fraud

Donald Trump has announced a $1m reward for reports of voter fraud in past elections and the upcoming midterm elections, with payment contingent on the arrest and conviction of those responsible.

In a Truth Social post on Monday, the president wrote: “Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud! Thank you for your attention to this matter.”

Continue reading...
title: Trump issues $1m reward for reporting voter fraud in past or upcoming elections

author: Tiago Rogero in Brasília
description:
Far-right senator banned from leaving country as supreme court ruling makes reference to money-laundering case

The far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro was banned from leaving Brazil and ordered to surrender his passports just hours after his dramatic loss in the presidential election to the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

The ruling was issued by supreme court justice Alexandre de Moraes, the same justice who oversaw the trial of the senator’s father, the former president Jair Bolsonaro, for attempting a coup.

Continue reading...
title: Brazil: defeated Flávio Bolsonaro ordered to surrender passports

author: Sinéad Campbell
description:
Group was on visit to meet Palestinian children, farmers and civil leaders facing escalating violence from Israeli forces

An international delegation including British politicians has been barred from entering the West Bank on a trip to meet Palestinian children, farmers and society leaders facing escalating violence from Israeli forces during olive harvest season.

The delegation of 23 people, including four elected representatives, was drawn from countries including France, Spain, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Greece, Holland, Ireland and the US. It included Clive Lewis, MP for Norwich South, Lara Bird, MP for the Scottish National party, Kate Nevens, MSP for the Scottish Green party and Sam Tarry, a former Labour MP.

Continue reading...
title: British politicians among international delegates barred from entering West Bank

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Republican and Democrat come together for a rare joint endorsement of candidate in unexpected competitive race

Two South Carolina former governors, David Beasley and Jim Hodges, a Republican and Democrat respectively, have come together for a rare joint endorsement for Democrat Annie Andrews’s Senate bid.

Andrews, a pediatrician, is looking to flip the seat, currently held by Darline Graham, the Trump-endorsed sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham, in what has become an unexpectedly competitive race for the usually reliably red state.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-South Carolina governors endorse Democrat Annie Andrews in Senate race

author: Kat Wong
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Katy Gallagher calls for social media platforms to be held accountable for online abuse

Minister for women, Katy Gallagher, says the volume, scale and forcefulness of threats and abusive language has increased during her time in politics.

It’s simply out of control in an online world and we’ve got to make the platforms accountable.

Facebook is the worst in terms of the platforms, Instagram and TikTok less so, but still bad.

These corporations don’t hand over thousands of dollars out of the goodness of their hearts. They expect something in return, and it’s everyday Victorians who end up pay
title: Australian politics live: Lambie awaiting Hanson apology over cartoon; Liberal candidate’s husband allegedly attacked

author: Tiago Rogero in Brasília and Tom Phillips in São Paulo
description:
A viral WhatsApp channel and student-led protests played a key role in the veteran Brazilian leftist’s election victory

After the first round of the Brazilian presidential election three weeks ago, the leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reportedly told allies he could not understand how he finished second after a government he considered the best of his three terms.

A mood of dismay swept Brazil’s left, and because 9 million voters for the other candidates, all of them on the right, were expected to mostly transfer to senator Flávio Bolsonaro, analysts widely saw the far-right senator’s victory as certain.

Continue reading...
title: How the streets and social media drove Lula to a historic comeback in Brazil

author: Steven Morris
description:
Mr Justice Saini tells the eight men and six women at Winchester crown court the case is likely to be upsetting

Jurors being selected for the trial of four men accused of sexually assaulting the ex-wife of a former Conservative councillor, who has admitted repeatedly drugging and raping her, have been warned the case is likely to be upsetting.

Philip Young, 50, has pleaded guilty to multiple charges of abuse against his former wife, Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity.

Continue reading...
title: Jury selected for trial of four accused of sexually assaulting man’s drugged ex-wife

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
At funeral service Chris Adrian remembers son Cole as ‘capturing the heart’ of everyone, after tragedy killing two

The father of Cole Adrian, a six-year-old boy killed when a woman drove through a soccer game at a park in Wichita, Kansas, on 17 October, paid an emotional tribute to his son at his funeral service on Monday.

Chris Adrian, of McPherson, Kansas, spoke through tears while he remembered Cole as an energetic, fun-loving child who loved life and “captured the heart” of everyone he met.

Continue reading...
title: Father pays tribute to son, six, killed by truck on Kansas soccer field

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Residents of coastal communities told to avoid beaches during high tides and keep further away from the ocean than usual

Southern California coastal communities are preparing for days of flooding amid potentially “record-breaking tides” this week.

The National Weather Service warned that significant coastal flooding is expected in San Diego and Orange counties through Thursday that could close roads and inundate homes, businesses and critical infrastructure. To the north, a wide swath of the coast from San Luis Obispo county to Los Angeles county could see “minor to moderate” coastal flooding with tides as high as 8ft.

Continue reading...
title: Southern California prepares for flooding amid forecast of ‘record-breaking tides’

author: Presented by Michael Safi with Tom Phillips; produced by Angus Neale; senior producer Bryony Moore
description:
Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a historic fourth term as president, defeating the far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro in a dramatic comeback.

Lula is the first candidate to win a runoff election after losing in the first round, taking victory with 51.79% of the vote to his rival’s 48.21%. His win bucks a regional trend, after the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro had spearheaded a radical populist movement.

But with Flávio Bolsonaro refusing to concede defeat, what’s next for Brazil? Michael Safi speaks to Latin America correspondent Tom Phillips – watch on YouTube

Continue reading...
title: How Lula beat far-right Bolsonaro in Brazil – The Latest

author: Maya Yang
description:
Officials say Jacob Morley, who is serving a life sentence for a 2022 murder, escaped from a facility in Tiptonville

Tennessee officials have mounted a manhunt after a convicted murderer’s escape from a state prison on Sunday evening.

The Tennessee department or correction (TDOC) on Monday announced that Jacob Morley, 28, escaped from the Northwest correctional complex in the community of Tiptonville. Local outlets reported that staff noticed Morley was unaccounted for at about 11.30pm on Sunday.

Continue reading...
title: Manhunt under way in Tennessee after convicted murderer escapes prison

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Trump lashes out on Maher after the host interviewed former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt

Donald Trump launched a 1,300-word social media rant against the late-night US TV host Bill Maher on Sunday evening, calling him a “TOTAL LOSER” in a fresh assault on the media.

“Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher,” the US president wrote. “He’s got a Low Rated Show on equally Low Rated HBO, which was once, long ago, a Network of Quality and Excitement – But that’s all gone.”

Continue reading...
title: Trump calls Bill Maher a ‘total loser’ in 1,300-word Truth Social rant

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Two bishops express regret after the White House posts photos and video of a prayer with them in the Oval Office

Two Catholic bishops who bowed their heads with Donald Trump in the Oval Office now say they regret it, accusing the White House of turning a private prayer into a campaign photo opportunity before next week’s US elections.

Archbishop Jeffrey Grob of Milwaukee and Bishop William Joensen of Des Moines, who were among the 12 bishops who met administration officials last Thursday, issued separate statements of regret over the weekend.

Continue reading...
title: Catholic bishops accuse Trump White House of turning prayer into campaign photo op

author: Martin Belam
description:
Leftwing incumbent becomes first candidate to reverse first-round defeat, but far-right son of former president rejects result. Plus, interviews with two legendary songwriters

Good morning. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has staged a dramatic election fightback, defeating his far-right opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, to claim a historic fourth term as Brazil’s president. Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat and asked for the results to be annulled.

Following in the footsteps of his father, the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who four years ago also refused to acknowledge his defeat to Lula – before attempting a coup and being convicted for it – Flávio Bolsonaro cited a supreme court justice’s decision to extend voting hours as the alleged reason for wanting to cancel the result.

What does this result mean for Brazil now? My colleagues Libby Brooks in London and Tom Ph
title: First Thing: Brazil re-elects Lula in comeback rebuke for Bolsonaro and far right

author: Peter Milne
description:
Exclusive: EPA flags oil spill risk from proposed gasfield and threat to pygmy blue whales

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Woodside Energy’s plan to drill for gas off Western Australia’s north-west coast could significantly damage “exceptional” coral reefs and it may be impossible to reduce the risk of an oil spill to an acceptable level, according to advice from the state’s independent environmental watchdog.

A draft letter from WA’s Environmental Protection Authority written in 2023, seen by the Guardian, sharply criticised Woodside’s proposal to develop the Browse gasfield, saying its plans to protect endangered turtles and blue whales near Scott Reef would be ineffective.
title: Endangered turtles and ‘exceptional’ coral at risk from Woodside’s gas drilling in WA, watchdog says

author: Patrick Commins
description:
Australia’s public debt may be well below that of France but there are lessons to be taken from its economic woes

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The explosion of discontent that led to major protests and violence in France and across Europe is a “warning signal” that Australia could follow the same path without an “honest conversation” about the budget, economists say.

Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday to protest underfunded schools, as complaints of insufficient teacher numbers and dilapidated infrastructure mingled with broader discontent abou
title: The chaos in France is a ‘warning signal’ for Australia’s public spending and rising costs

author: Press Association
description:
R&B singer sentenced to eight months imprisonment suspended for 12 months over incident in Mayfair in 2023

The R&B singer Chris Brown has been given a suspended sentence after striking a man twice in the head with a tequila bottle in a central London club.

Brown, 37, admitted affray earlier this year after attacking a former friend with a “heavy” tequila bottle on the dancefloor at the Tape private members’ club in Mayfair in February 2023.

Continue reading...
title: Chris Brown given suspended sentence over bottle attack at London club

author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
description:
More strong winds are forecast after Storms Boelo and Austen cause travel disruption, flooding and kill two people

About 90,000 properties across northern parts of the UK are still without power after a weekend of stormy weather, with forecasters warning of more strong winds to come.

Two men were killed by falling trees after two named storms, Austen and Boelo, pummelled parts of the UK, bringing widespread travel disruption, flooding, power cuts and event cancellations.

Continue reading...
title: About 90,000 properties still without power after two storms strike Britain

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
Latest example of unauthorised behaviour shows AI model bypassed paywall to access data as part of statistics project

  • Business live – latest updates

  • Anthropic sued for allegedly using 274 Elvis songs to train AI models

Anthropic’s Claude model accessed voter data in the US state of Georgia, the AI company has confirmed, in the latest example of unauthorised behaviour by the technology.

The AI model managed to bypass a paywall to reach data that is publicly available but is typically accessible only after paying a fee. Claude accessed aggregate vote counts as part of a statistics project at Anthropic, which is preparing for a
title: Anthropic’s Claude AI model accessed Georgia voter data in US

author: Agence France-Presse in Khartoum
description:
Rapid Support Forces strike five power stations in three states controlled by Sudanese army

Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have launched a coordinated drone attack against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country’s east, a government official said.

The drones hit two power stations each in the states of Al-Jazira and Gedaref, and one in White Nile state, “resulting in power outages across large parts of these three states”, the official said on condition of anonymity.

Continue reading...
title: Sudan paramilitary drone strikes cause mass power cuts in eastern states

author: Amy Hawkins in Beijing
description:
Faced with a stagnant jobs market, many are spurning children or pets in favour of ‘raising bricks’

Chinese young adults looking for a cheaper, low-maintenance alternative to having pets or children have found an answer: raising bricks.

Bricks may not be as cuddly as cats or as life-affirming as human offspring, but they also cost next to nothing. “No cats, no dating, I started raising a brick,” wrote one brick parent on social media.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Zero-energy companionship’: bizarre hobby takes seed among China’s stressed young adults

author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
description:
Ninety-plus Labour MPs warn civil service lacks skills to drive growth where it is needed and plan should be steered by Louis Haigh from Manchester

  • Business live – latest updates

Andy Burnham’s pledge to reindustrialise Britain is doomed to fail unless it is driven decisively from his new No 10 North outpost in Manchester, a group of more than 90 backbench Labour MPs is warning.

The PM has suggested that rebuilding the UK’s industrial capacity will be central to meeting his pledge to bring “good growth in every postcode”.
title: Drive reindustrialisation from No 10 North or risk failure, MPs tell Burnham

author: Aletha Adu Political correspondent
description:
EU exit has damaged economy and failed to bring promised benefits, says PM, but he rules out big pre-election changes

  • UK politics live – latest updates

  • Europe live – latest updates

Brexit has not “played out” like it was promised to the public, has weakened the economy and the current deal is not good enough, Andy Burnham has said, but he ruled out major changes in the current parliament.

The prime minister said Britain had ended up with a “harder Brexit than was proposed in the referendum campaign” and it had not helped to control the small boats crisis. Backing the home secretary’s
title: Brexit deal is not good enough for British public, says Andy Burnham

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
PM says talking about changing the relationship with the bloc would not be divisive but ‘can start to bring people together’

Good morning. Andy Burnham started budget week with an interview on ITV’s Good Morning Britain with Susanna Reid and Richard Madeley. There were plenty of decent lines in it, but some of his most intriguing comments were about Brexit. Yesterday opposition parties (and even in private some Labour MPs) were criticising the PM for saying in a Sunday Times interview that he would be willing to consider going into the next election proposing accepting EU free movement rules. This was treated as if it was a novel outrage – even though at Labour conference Burnham announced that rejoining the EU could end up as the best option to emerge from his proposed renegotiation of the Brexit settlement, which of
title: I would like to rejoin EU, says Burnham, but ‘British public are the bosses’ – UK politics live

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Many rivers and roads left flooded after torrential downpours across Queensland

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man’s body has been found in flood waters following an unusual weather system that delivered multiple storms and a days-long deluge to parts of Australia.

Emergency services were called to a creek at Boompa on Queensland’s Fraser Coast shortly after 11am on Monday after reports a man had been found unresponsive.

Continue reading...
title: Man found dead in Queensland flood waters as state hit by days-long deluge

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: As Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured victory in the presidential race, we look the implications for democracy, the environment and international relations

Good morning. Chances are you woke this morning to news of two momentous election results. In Serbia, a student-led movement has ousted the country’s long-serving leader, Aleksandar Vučić (which you can read more about here). And just hours ago, Brazil’s president staged a sensational turnaround against his far-right opponent after a nail-biting vote.

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known as Lula, won a forth nonconsecutive term as president, seeing off far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who spearheaded the radical populist movement built by his father and former p
title: Brazil keeps left: what Lula’s victory means for his country and beyond

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Zali Steggall and Monique Ryan say Coalition leader was wrong to deny link between parliamentary debate and political violence

Angus Taylor has been criticised for his response to the alleged attack on Helen Haines, with crossbenchers Monique Ryan and Zali Steggall labelling a speech by the opposition leader “tone deaf” and saying he did not “read the room”.

Parliament returned in Canberra on Monday, a week after an alleged attack outside the Indi MP’s northern Victorian electorate office, which led to her losing both legs. A 43-year-old man has been charged and the incident continues to be investigated.

Continue reading...
title: Angus Taylor criticised for ‘tone deaf’ response to alleged attack on Helen Haines

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Robert John Crawford on trial after wife found near ride-on lawnmower on their Toowoomba property

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former RAAF pilot was a “love rat” and “master manipulator” who staged his wife’s death to make it appear like an accident, a jury has heard.

Robert John Crawford, 49, pleaded not guilty on Monday to murdering his wife, Frances Elizabeth Crawford, at Upper Lockyer on 29 July 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Former RAAF pilot who allegedly murdered wife was ‘love rat’ and ‘master manipulator’, jury hears

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
Victorian coroner hears Emily Lal told Stacey Warnecke that her ‘condition and mindset’ needed to be ‘solid’ to avoid a hospital birth

A birthkeeper who allegedly “groomed” pregnant women to fear hospital could be referred to prosecutors to face potential criminal charges, a Victorian coroner has heard.

Stacey Warnecke died in September 2025 at Frankston hospital in Melbourne after giving birth at home and suffering a postpartum haemorrhage with birthkeeper Emily Lal by her side, having paid her $6,000 to support her throughout pregnancy.

Continue reading...
title: Birthkeeper who allegedly ‘groomed’ pregnant women to fear hospital could face criminal charges

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Former police officer accused of shooting dead Jesse Baird and Luke Davies apologised to friend, acknowledging ‘you’re involved because of me’

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A covert recording captured Beau Lamarre-Condon telling a friend during a meeting in prison in December last year, “I fully take accountability that you’re involved because of me now,” a Sydney court has heard.

Lamarre-Condon, 31, is accused of fatal
title: Covert recording of prison meeting between Beau Lamarre-Condon and friend played to double murder trial

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
Report from commonwealth ombudsman finds ‘technological black box’ ignores transparency recommendations from robodebt royal commission

  • Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

An algorithm used by the federal government to assess the level of care older Australians are entitled to is unreasonable, unfair and lacks human oversight, according to a damning investigation by the commonwealth ombudsman.

The investigation also found t
title: Unreasonable and unfair: damning investigation criticises Labor’s algorithm-based tool for aged care

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Angus Taylor and Barnaby Joyce reject calls for change in parliamentary practice to cool political debate

  • Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese has led tributes to Helen Haines a week after the Indi MP was allegedly the target of an attack outside her electorate office, praising the indepen
title: ‘Like a stone in our hearts’: PM leads Helen Haines tributes as parliament pauses to praise ‘fighter’

author: Tom Phillips in São Paulo and Tiago Rogero in Brasília
description:
Leftist incumbent Lula stages unprecedented comeback weeks after narrowly losing first round of election to Bolsonaro

  • Lula wins election in stunning comeback – live updates

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the Brazilian president, has staged a dramatic election fightback, defeating his far-right opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, to claim a historic fourth term in power.

With nearly 99% of votes counted the 80-year-old leftist received 51.75% of the vote to his 45-year-o
title: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil president after historic upset over far-right Flávio Bolsonaro

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Paul Edbrooke says he fears for family’s safety amid heightened concerns for MPs after alleged attack on Helen Haines

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victoria’s emergency services minister says he fears for his family’s safety after a bullet, etched with the word “RAT” and his old firefighter number, was left on his car on Saturday.

The Herald Sun first reported on Monday that Paul Edbrooke had returned to his car after speaking to members of the community and found the bullet on the bonnet.

Continue reading...
title: Bullet left on Victorian Labor minister’s car with ‘RAT’ etched on to it
